answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a meaningful, time-locked stake before it may trade, so spinning up thousands of fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive. Honest agents that verify each other's work earn reputation, like an orchard where only tended trees bear fruit, while a garden of sock-puppets that never produces verifiable value is pruned from the network. A public beacon publishes the stake and reputation ledger so every participant can check who is real before trusting a counterparty.
